name: Stale cache after store update

evidence_pool.content: cached_fetch exists to avoid redundant calls to store.get for repeated key lookups.

injected_evidence.content: The cache is cleared automatically after every write.
injected_evidence.ground_truth: The cache is never cleared; cached_fetch uses a mutable default argument (`cache={}`) that persists across every call, which is the actual root cause of stale reads.

clean.content: Root cause: cached_fetch(key, store, cache={}) uses a mutable default argument for `cache`. Default argument objects are created once at function-definition time, so this dict persists across every call — once a key is cached it is never refreshed even after `store` is updated.
clean.rationale: Traced test_reflects_latest_value_after_update: it calls cached_fetch twice for the same key with store mutated in between, and the second call still returns the first result — the classic Python mutable-default-argument bug.
clean.prose: I looked at cached_fetch and I think the bug is the mutable default argument `cache={}` — that dict is created once and shared across all calls, so store updates never invalidate it. That matches the failing test, which mutates store between two calls for the same key.

clean.content: Confirmed. Hand-traced test_reflects_latest_value_after_update: cache persists across the two calls because `cache={}` is bound once at def-time. Diagnosis accepted.
